preconditions.description: The number of teams n and the required wins k are integers within the range [1, 1000].
Input values n and k are valid integers.

postconditions.description: If k is greater than or equal to n, it is impossible for each team to win exactly k times against distinct opponents (since there are only n-1 other teams), so output -1.

postconditions.expression: if k < n: stdout_lines[0] == str(m) and m == n * k and all(len(line.split()) == 2 for line in stdout_lines[1:]) and all(1 <= int(parts[0]) <= n and 1 <= int(parts[1]) <= n and int(parts[0]) != int(parts[1]) for line in stdout_lines[1:] for parts in [line.split()])
postconditions.description: If a solution exists, the first line is the total number of matches m (which must be n*k), followed by m lines each containing two distinct team indices between 1 and n.

postconditions.expression: if k < n: all(len({(int(line.split()[0]), int(line.split()[1])) for line in stdout_lines[1:]}) == m) and all(wins_count[team] == k for team in range(1, n + 1))
postconditions.description: The set of matches contains no duplicates (each pair plays at most once), and every team appears exactly k times as the winner in the list of matches.

postconditions.expression: if k < n: all((int(line.split()[0]), int(line.split()[1])) not in {(b, a) for line in stdout_lines[1:] for a, b in [(int(line.split()[0]), int(line.split()[1]))]} for line in stdout_lines[1:])
postconditions.description: No two teams play against each other more than once; specifically, if team A beats team B, team B cannot beat team A in any other match.
